result: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"MA","level":"state","category":"just_cause_eviction","title":"Reprisal against tenants for protected activity prohibited","requirement":"A landlord or agent may not threaten or take reprisals against a residential tenant who enforces housing laws in a judicial or administrative action, reports a health, building or housing code violation to a board of health or to the landlord, or organizes or joins a tenants' union. A reprisal makes the landlord liable for damages of at least one and at most three months' rent, or the tenant's actual damages if greater, plus costs and reasonable attorney's fees. A notice of termination of tenancy, rent increase or substantial change in tenancy terms received within six months after the protected activity is presumed to be a reprisal. The landlord can rebut the presumption only by clear and convincing evidence of independent justification.
